confidence_notes: Restaurant anchors rest on several sources that roughly agree (Numbeo, Wise, KoronaPay, a Cyprus-wide survey), but some are crowdsourced or dated, and Numbeo's page has user comments flagging outdated data. Drink anchors are weaker: the cappuccino figure is well corroborated, but beer and cocktail come from a mix of menus, aggregators and an undated café-bar review, and the wine glass is derived from the local beer relationship because the only direct wine figure (EUR 2) is undated and likely stale. Cocktail uses a beer-relationship basis (about 2.5x a draft beer) with the undated 'from EUR 5' review as a floor. Accommodation anchors are holistic model estimates for July peak season; no live booking pages or listings were inspected. EUR figures were converted to USD at about 1.17, implied by Wise's USD figures for Paphos; no live exchange rate was checked. The fx observation is the most recent one the search surfaced (20 March 2026, about seven months before the generation date), not a confirmed latest value; the rate was reported in search output and I did not open the RBA page or its CSV to verify it.
comparable_city_reasoning: Anchored to Paphos-specific restaurant data (Numbeo: inexpensive meal about EUR 15, three-course dinner for two about EUR 60, cappuccino about EUR 3.24, domestic draft about EUR 3.50; cross-checked against Wise USD figures and a Cyprus-wide survey indicating lower meal prices, and KoronaPay's Numbeo-based summary). Drinks use the same local price level. Accommodation is a holistic estimate benchmarked to coastal southern European resort towns in July peak season, with Paphos treated as a relatively affordable Cypriot resort.
